caption_en:
4 claims. 3,000 years. Not all of them hold up.

Philistines and Palestinians: same people? 4 claims, fact checked.

1. The Philistines were Greeks from Crete? Close. A Sea People from the Aegean. Ramesses III fought them around 1177 BCE; the Peleset settled Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron and Gath. Ashkelon DNA: their European ancestry faded within about two centuries.
2. Palestinians are the Philistines? No. The Philistines vanished after Babylon destroyed Ashkelon in 604 BCE. Only the name survived: Herodotus wrote "Palaistine" in the 5th century BCE.
3. Julius Caesar renamed Judea? No. After the Bar Kokhba revolt (132 to 135 CE), Rome under Hadrian renamed the province Syria Palaestina.
4. Palestinians mostly migrated under Ottoman and British rule? No. Some did, but British reports found most Arab growth came from births.

Not perfect either: "Palestinians are Canaanites who were here before the Jews" is also a myth. Jews descend from the Israelites, who emerged from within Canaan. Two peoples with real roots, one borrowed name.

Sources: Feldman et al., Science Advances 2019; Agranat-Tamir et al., Cell 2020; Britannica; W. Eck; D. Grossman; Peel Commission 1937; Babylonian Chronicle.
Photos (Wikimedia Commons): Olaf Tausch, CC BY 3.0; Marie-Lan Nguyen, public domain; Webscribe, CC BY-SA 3.0.

transcript.heard: Four claims, 3,000 years. Egypt fights invaders from the sea. The Pelissates settle Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, and Dath. Claim one. Palestinians are the Philistines? No. The Philistines came from the Aegean. Their European DNA faded in two centuries. 604 BCE. Babylon destroys Ashkelon. Only the name survived. Claim two. Palestinians are Canaanites here before the Jews. They're Levantine Arabs, closest to Jordanians and Lebanese. Some ancient local DNA, yes, like their neighbors. A Canaanite people, no. Claim 3. Jews are foreigners from Europe. No roots here? No. Egypt named Israel in 1208 BCE, before the Philistines. Jewish DNA worldwide shows Levantine roots. Claim 4. The Romans named it Palestine to erase the Jews, partly. After the Bar-Kukba revolt, Hadrian made Judea Syria-Palestina, a punishment. The name was older. Herodotus used it. People's carry Canaanite roots one borrowed name so next time someone asks
